title: Questão 4 - ENEM 2025
context:
How is Dune so prescient about climate change?

The planet, or what’s left of it, is barely recognizable.
Once verdant, it’s now a parched wasteland. The rich shelter
in air-conditioned bubbles, leaving everyone else to face
the storms and sand.

This vision of climate apocalypse is all too familiar today,
but in 1963, when Frank Herbert started serializing his
science-fiction epic Dune, it was deeply strange. Mr. Herbert’s
tale of climate change no longer seems odd. It is in many ways
the story of our time.

How did Mr. Herbert foresee our predicament?
The environmentalism of Dune had a source close to
home. Native communities had suffered some of the worst
environmental harms in the midcentury United States,
and Mr. Herbert had close contacts among the Quileute
and Hoh peoples of the Olympic Peninsula in Washington
State. Indigenous environmentalists alerted him to how
much damage industrialism had wrought. They warned him
that it could become planetary in scope, a warning that he
passed on in his influential novel.
